title: Spread by Jesús I. Valles at Intar Theatre #spreadtheplay #jesusvalle...
transcript: You could not pay me to go back to ninth grade. Once is more than enough, but this new play called Spread by Jesús Valles shows that it is a beautiful experience, in its own right. A coming-of-age story about four ninth grade boys, this play mostly takes place in a single classroom where they have lunch together and concoct spread, a hodgepodge of different commissary foods. There are also some transitional scenes that provide glimpses into their lives at home, and what they're going through that they don't necessarily share with each other. This play is about a lot of things — friendship dynamics, the pressures of early adulthood coming into view, and the dauntingly confusing process of figuring out who you are. These concepts have certainly been tackled before, but I found this play anything but recycled. The characters are well-written, they're specific, and the acting is really great across the board. Teenagers are notoriously moody and hormonal, and it's easy for their interactions to become altercations, and I felt like everyone in the cast captured this really well. The way that the energy in the room turns on a dime feels totally realistic and it's part of what makes the piece so captivating. As a one-act, small-cast play in a small room (but with strategically multifunctional set pieces), I thought this production did a great job rendering a story that's both somewhat universal and granular. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Creator praises writing, acting, and direction with no significant caveats, calling it captivating and anything but recycled.
